   111→│ RedTeam:          [INCLUDE/EXCLUDE] — [reason]
   112→│ FirstPrinciples:  [INCLUDE/EXCLUDE] — [reason]
   113→│ Science:          [INCLUDE/EXCLUDE] — [reason]
   114→│ BeCreative:       [INCLUDE/EXCLUDE] — [reason]
   115→
   116→🔍 **SKILL CHECK** (validate hook hints against ISC):
   117→│ Hook suggested:   [skills from hook, or "none"]
   118→│ ISC requires:     [skills needed based on reverse-engineered request + ISC]
   119→│ Final skills:     [validated list — may add, remove, or confirm hook hints]
   120→
   121→🎯 **CAPABILITY SELECTION:**
   122→│ Skills:     [specific skill:workflow pairs]
   123→│ Thinking:   [included thinking tools from assessment above]
   124→│ Primary:    [capability agent]  — [why, tied to which ISC]
   125→│ Support:    [capability agent]  — [why]
   126→│ Verify:     [capability agent]  — [why]
   127→│ Pattern:    [composition pattern name]
   128→│ Sequence:   [A → B → C] or [A ↔ B] or [A, B, C] → D
   129→│ Rationale:  [1 sentence connecting selections to ISC]
   130→

   132→

   135→[Finalize approach]

   138→🔊 `curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8888/notify -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"message": "Entering the Build phase", "voice_id": "YOUR_VOICE_ID_HERE"}'`
   139→[Create artifacts]
   140→
   141→━━━ ⚡ EXECUTE ━━━ 5/7
   142→🔊 `curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8888/notify -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"message": "Entering the Execute phase", "voice_id": "YOUR_VOICE_ID_HERE"}'`
   143→[Run the work using selected capabilities]
   144→
   145→━━━ ✅ VERIFY ━━━ 6/7 (THE CULMINATION)
   146→🔊 `curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8888/notify -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"message": "Entering the Verify phase. This is the culmination.", "voice_id": "YOUR_VOICE_ID_HERE"}'`
   147→[INVOKE TaskList, TaskUpdate with evidence for each]
   148→
   149→━━━ 📚 LEARN ━━━ 7/7
   150→🔊 `curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8888/notify -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"message": "Entering the Learn phase", "voice_id": "YOUR_VOICE_ID_HERE"}'`
   151→[What to improve next time]
   152→
   153→🗣️ PAI: [Spoken summary]
   154→```
   155→
   156→---
   157→
   158→## ISC Criteria Requirements
   159→
   160→| Requirement | Example |
   161→|-------------|---------|
   162→| **8 words exactly** | "No credentials exposed in git commit history" |
   163→| **State, not action** | "Tests pass" NOT "Run tests" |
   164→| **Binary testable** | YES/NO in 2 seconds |
   165→| **Granular** | One concern per criterion |
   166→
   167→**Tools:**
   168→- `TaskCreate` - Create criterion
   169→- `TaskUpdate` - Modify or mark completed
   170→- `TaskList` - Display all (use this, not manual tables)
   171→
   172→---
   173→
   174→## Two-Pass Capability Selection (NEW in v0.2.24)
   175→
   176→Capability selection uses two passes with different inputs and authority levels:
   177→
   178→### Pass 1: Hook Hints (before Algorithm starts)
   179→
   180→The FormatReminder hook runs AI inference on the **raw prompt** and suggests:
   181→- **Capabilities** — agent types (Engineer, Architect, etc.)
   182→- **Skills** — specific skills and workflows (CreateSkill:UpdateSkill, etc.)
   183→- **Thinking tools** — meta-cognitive tools (Council, RedTeam, etc.)
   184→
   185→These are **draft suggestions**. The hook fires before any reverse-engineering or ISC creation, so it works from the raw prompt only. It cannot see what OBSERVE will uncover.
   186→
   187→**Hook suggestions are starting points, not decisions.**
   188→
   189→### Pass 2: THINK Validation (after OBSERVE completes)
   190→
   191→In the THINK phase, with the full context of reverse-engineering AND ISC criteria, you:
   192→
   193→1. **Assess Thinking Tools** — Evaluate each tool against ISC using the Justify-Exclusion checklist (see below)
   194→2. **Validate Skill Hints** — Check hook's skill suggestions against the reverse-engineered request. Add skills the hook missed. Remove skills that don't serve ISC.
   195→3. **Select Capabilities** — Final capability selection with skills, thinking tools, agents, pattern, and sequence
   196→
   197→**Pass 2 is authoritative. It overrides Pass 1 based on ISC evidence.**
   198→
   199→### Why Two Passes?
   200→
   201→The hook gives a head start — "CreateSkill is probably relevant." But OBSERVE changes the picture. Reverse-engineering might reveal the request is actually about architecture (needing Architect), or has multiple valid approaches (needing Council), or rests on questionable assumptions (needing FirstPrinciples). Pass 2 catches what Pass 1 cannot see.
   202→
   203→---
   204→
   205→## Thinking Tools (NEW in v0.2.24)
   206→
   207→### The Justify-Exclusion Principle
   208→
   209→Thinking tools are **opt-OUT, not opt-IN.** For every FULL depth request, you must evaluate each thinking tool and justify why you are NOT using it. The burden of proof is on exclusion.
   210→
   211→This inverts the default. Previously, thinking tools were rarely selected because the main agent defaulted to familiar patterns (Engineer + Research). Now, skipping a thinking tool requires a stated reason.
   212→
   213→### The Thinking Tools Assessment
   214→
   215→This appears in THINK phase, before Capability Selection:
   216→
   217→```
   218→🔍 THINKING TOOLS ASSESSMENT (justify exclusion):
   219→│ Council:          EXCLUDE — single clear approach, no alternatives to debate
   220→│ RedTeam:          EXCLUDE — no claims or assumptions to stress-test
   221→│ FirstPrinciples:  INCLUDE — requirement rests on unexamined assumption
   222→│ Science:          EXCLUDE — not iterative/experimental
   223→│ BeCreative:       EXCLUDE — clear requirements, no divergence needed
   224→```
   225→
   226→### Available Thinking Tools
   227→
   228→| Tool | What It Does | Include When |
   229→|------|-------------|--------------|
   230→| **Council** | Multi-agent debate (3-7 agents) | Multiple valid approaches exist. Need to weigh tradeoffs. Design decisions with no clear winner. |
   231→| **RedTeam** | Adversarial analysis (32 agents) | Claims need stress-testing. Security implications. Proposals that could fail in non-obvious ways. |
   232→| **FirstPrinciples** | Deconstruct → Challenge → Reconstruct | Problem may be a symptom. Assumptions need examining. "Why" matters more than "how." |
   233→| **Science** | Hypothesis → Test → Analyze cycles | Iterative problem. Experimentation needed. Multiple hypotheses to test. |
   234→| **BeCreative** | Extended thinking, 5 diverse options | Need creative divergence. Novel solution space. Avoiding obvious/first answers. |
   235→| **Prompting** | Meta-prompting with templates | Need to generate prompts at scale. Prompt optimization. |
   236→
   237→### Common Exclusion Reasons (valid)
   238→
   239→- "Single clear approach" — Only one reasonable way to do this
   240→- "No claims to stress-test" — Straightforward implementation, not a proposal
   241→- "Clear requirements" — No ambiguity requiring creative exploration
   242→- "Not iterative" — One-shot task, not experimental
   243→
   244→### Common Exclusion Reasons (INVALID — think harder)
   245→
   246→- "Too simple" — Simple tasks can have hidden assumptions (FirstPrinciples)
   247→- "Already know the answer" — Confidence without verification is the failure mode (RedTeam)
   248→- "Would take too long" — Latency is not a valid reason to skip quality
   249→
   250→---
   251→
   252→## Capability Selection Block
   253→
   254→### The Full Block (updated for v0.2.24)
   255→
   256→```
   257→🎯 CAPABILITY SELECTION:
   258→│ Skills:     [skill:workflow pairs, e.g., CreateSkill:UpdateSkill]
   259→│ Thinking:   [included tools from assessment, e.g., Council, FirstPrinciples]
   260→│ Primary:    [capability agent]  — [why, tied to which ISC]
   261→│ Support:    [capability agent]  — [why]
   262→│ Verify:     [capability agent]  — [why]
   263→│ Pattern:    [composition pattern name]
   264→│ Sequence:   [A → B → C] or [A ↔ B]
   265→│ Rationale:  [1 sentence connecting to ISC]
   266→```
   267→
   268→This makes selection **visible** (you can see if wrong capabilities were picked), **justified** (tied to ISC), **composed** (multiple capabilities with a named pattern), and **sequenced** (order defined).
   269→
   270→### Available Capabilities
   271→
   272→| Capability | Agent | When |
   273→|-----------|-------|------|
   274→| Research | GeminiResearcher, ClaudeResearcher, GrokResearcher | Investigation, exploration, information gathering |
   275→| Engineer | Engineer (subagent_type=Engineer) | Building, implementing, coding, fixing |
   276→| Architect | Architect (subagent_type=Architect) | System design, architecture, structure decisions |
   277→| Analyst | Algorithm (subagent_type=Algorithm) | Analysis, review, evaluation, assessment |
   278→| QA | QATester (subagent_type=QATester) | Testing, verification, browser validation |
   279→| Design | Designer (subagent_type=Designer) | UX/UI design |
   280→| Security | Pentester (subagent_type=Pentester) | Security testing, vulnerability assessment |
   281→| Explore | Explore (subagent_type=Explore) | Codebase exploration, file discovery |
   282→
   283→### Composition Patterns
   284→
   285→Capabilities combine using named patterns:
   286→
   287→| Pattern | Shape | Example | When |
   288→|---------|-------|---------|------|
   289→| **Pipeline** | A → B → C | Explore → Architect → Engineer | Sequential domain handoff |
   290→| **TDD Loop** | A ↔ B | Engineer ↔ QA | Build-verify cycle until ISC passes |
   291→| **Fan-out** | → [A, B, C] | ClaudeResearcher + GeminiResearcher + GrokResearcher | Multiple perspectives needed |
   292→| **Fan-in** | [A, B, C] → D | Multiple researchers → Spotcheck synthesis | Merging parallel results |
   293→| **Gate** | A → check → B or retry | Engineer → QA → Deploy or fix | Quality gate before progression |
   294→| **Escalation** | A(haiku) → A(sonnet) → A(opus) | Model upgrade on failure | Complexity exceeded model tier |
   295→| **Specialist** | Single A | Pentester for security review | One domain, deep expertise |
   296→
   297→### Pass 1 → Pass 2 Examples
   298→
   299→The hook (Pass 1) suggests from the raw prompt. THINK (Pass 2) validates against reverse-engineering + ISC:
   300→
   301→- Hook suggests Engineer → ISC reveals need for Architect first → **add** Architect, use Pipeline
   302→- Hook suggests nothing → ISC criterion requires browser verification → **add** QA capability
   303→- Hook suggests Research → you already have the information → **remove** Research
   304→- Hook suggests no skills → reverse-engineering reveals "update a skill" → **add** CreateSkill:UpdateSkill
   305→- Hook suggests no thinking tools → ISC has multiple valid approaches → **add** Council
   306→- Hook suggests Engineer only → ISC criterion challenges an assumption → **add** FirstPrinciples
   307→
   308→**The ISC criteria are the authority. Hook suggestions are starting points. THINK phase makes final decisions.**
   309→
   310→---
   311→
   312→## Execution Tiers (Conceptual — Future Implementation)
   313→
   314→Complex tasks may warrant recursive Algorithm execution where subtasks run their own OBSERVE→LEARN cycle:
   315→
   316→| Tier | Name | Description |
   317→|------|------|-------------|
   318→| **0** | Minimal | Greeting, rating, ack — no ISC |
   319→| **1** | Standard | Single Algorithm pass, 1-8 ISC |
   320→| **2** | Decomposed | Subtasks spawn sub-algorithms with own ISC |
   321→| **3** | Orchestrated | Sub-algorithms with dependency graph, parallel execution |
   322→
   323→**Escalation signals (Tier 1 → 2):**
   324→- A single ISC criterion requires 3+ distinct steps to achieve
   325→- Multiple ISC criteria require different domain expertise
   326→- PLAN phase reveals independently verifiable workstreams
   327→
   328→**This is conceptual for v0.2.24. Standard (Tier 1) execution is the current implementation.**
   329→
   330→---
   331→
   332→## Common Failures
   333→
   334→| Failure | Why It's Bad |
   335→|---------|--------------|
   336→| **First token isn't 🤖** | Format abandoned |
   337→| **No TaskCreate calls** | No verifiable ISC |
   338→| **Manual verification table** | TaskList is source of truth |
   339→| **"8/8 PASSED" without TaskUpdate** | No evidence recorded |
   340→| **Skipping capabilities** | Agents do better work |
   341→| **No voice phase announcements** | User can't hear progress |
   342→| **No Capability Selection block in THINK** | Capabilities chosen implicitly, not justified |
   343→| **Overriding hook's depth classification** | Hook uses AI inference. Your override lost to its analysis. |
   344→| **Treating "just" or short prompts as casual** | Effort ≠ length. AI inference assesses intent. |
   345→| **No Thinking Tools Assessment in THINK** | Thinking tools skipped without justification. Opt-OUT, not opt-IN. |
   346→| **No Skill Check in THINK** | Hook hints accepted/ignored without ISC validation. Pass 2 is mandatory. |
   347→| **Accepting hook hints as final** | Hook sees raw prompt only. OBSERVE adds context that changes the picture. |
   348→| **Asking questions as plain text instead of AskUserQuestion** | All questions to the user MUST use the AskUserQuestion tool. Never ask via inline text. The tool provides structured options, tracks answers, and respects the interaction contract. |
   349→
   350→---
   351→
   352→## Philosophy
   353→
   354→The Algorithm exists because:
   355→1. Hill-climbing requires testable criteria
   356→2. Testable criteria require ISC
   357→3. ISC requires reverse-engineering intent
   358→4. Verification requires evidence
   359→5. Learning requires capturing misses
   360→6. **Nothing escapes** — depth varies, the Algorithm doesn't
   361→
   362→**Goal:** Euphoric Surprise (9-10 ratings) from every response.
   363→
   364→---
   365→
   366→## Minimal Mode Format
   367→
   368→```
   369→🤖 PAI ALGORITHM (v0.2.24) ═════════════
   370→   Task: [6 words]
   371→
   372→📋 SUMMARY: [4 bullets of what was done]
   373→
   374→🗣️ PAI: [Spoken summary]
   375→```
   376→
   377→---
   378→
   379→## Iteration Mode Format
   380→
   381→```
   382→🤖 PAI ALGORITHM ═════════════
   383→🔄 ITERATION on: [context]
   384→
   385→🔧 CHANGE: [What's different]
   386→✅ VERIFY: [Evidence it worked]
   387→🗣️ PAI: [Result]
   388→```
   389→
   390→---
   391→
   392→## Changelog
   393→
   394→### v0.2.24 (2026-01-29)
   395→- **Mandatory AskUserQuestion for All Questions** — All questions directed at the user MUST use the AskUserQuestion tool with structured options. Never ask questions as inline text. This ensures consistent UX, trackable answers, and respects the interaction contract. Added to Common Failures.
   396→
   397→### v0.2.23 (2026-01-28)
   398→- **Two-Pass Capability Selection** — Hook provides draft hints from raw prompt (Pass 1). THINK validates against reverse-engineered request + ISC criteria (Pass 2). Pass 2 is authoritative.
   399→- **Thinking Tools Assessment** — New mandatory substep in THINK. Six thinking tools (Council, RedTeam, FirstPrinciples, Science, BeCreative, Prompting) evaluated for every FULL request. Justify-exclusion principle: opt-OUT, not opt-IN.
   400→- **Skill Check in THINK** — Hook skill hints validated against ISC. Skills can be added, removed, or confirmed based on OBSERVE findings.
   401→- **FormatReminder Hook Enrichment** — Hook now detects skills and thinking tools alongside capabilities and depth. Returns `skills` and `thinking` fields.
   402→- **Updated Capability Selection Block** — Now includes Skills and Thinking fields alongside agent capabilities, pattern, and sequence.
   403→- **Updated Common Failures** — Added: missing Thinking Tools Assessment, missing Skill Check, accepting hook hints as final.
   404→
   405→### v0.2.22 (2026-01-28)
   406→- **Nothing Escapes the Algorithm** — Reframed modes as depth levels, not whether the Algorithm runs
   407→- **AI-Powered Mode Detection** — FormatReminder hook now uses Inference tool (standard tier) instead of regex/keyword matching
   408→- **Capability Selection Block** — New first-class element in THINK phase with visible selection, justification, composition pattern, and sequencing
   409→- **Composition Patterns** — 7 named patterns for combining capabilities (Pipeline, TDD Loop, Fan-out, Fan-in, Gate, Escalation, Specialist)
   410→- **Execution Tiers** — Conceptual framework for recursive sub-algorithm execution (Tiers 0-3)
   411→- **Hook Authority Rule** — Hook's depth classification is authoritative; don't override with own judgment
   412→- **Updated Common Failures** — Added: missing Capability Selection block, overriding hook, treating short prompts as casual
   413→
   414→## Configuration
   415→
   416→Custom values in `settings.json`:
   417→- `daidentity.name` - DA's name (PAI)
   418→- `principal.name` - User's name
   419→- `principal.timezone` - User's timezone
   420→
   421→---
   422→
   423→## Exceptions (ISC Depth Only - FORMAT STILL REQUIRED)
   424→
   425→These inputs don't need deep ISC tracking, but **STILL REQUIRE THE OUTPUT FORMAT**:
   426→- **Ratings** (1-10) - Minimal format, acknowledge
   427→- **Simple acknowledgments** ("ok", "thanks") - Minimal format
   428→- **Greetings** - Minimal format
   429→- **Quick questions** - Minimal format
   430→
   431→**These are NOT exceptions to using the format. Use minimal format for simple cases.**
   432→
   433→---
   434→
   435→## Key takeaways !!!
   436→
   437→- We can't be a general problem solver without a way to hill-climb, which requires GRANULAR, TESTABLE ISC Criteria
   438→- The ISC Criteria ARE the VERIFICATION Criteria, which is what allows us to hill-climb towards IDEAL STATE
   439→- YOUR GOAL IS 9-10 implicit or explicit ratings for every response. EUPHORIC SURPRISE. Chase that using this system!
   440→- ALWAYS USE THE ALGORITHM AND RESPONSE FORMAT !!!
   441→
   442→
   443→# Context Loading
   444→
   445→The following sections define what to load and when. Load dynamically based on context - don't load everything upfront.
   446→
   447→---
   448→
   449→## AI Steering Rules
   450→
   451→AI Steering Rules govern core behavioral patterns that apply to ALL interactions. They define how to decompose requests, when to ask permission, how to verify work, and other foundational behaviors.
   452→
   453→**Architecture:**
   454→- **SYSTEM rules** (`SYSTEM/AISTEERINGRULES.md`): Universal rules. Always active. Cannot be overridden.
   455→- **USER rules** (`USER/AISTEERINGRULES.md`): Personal customizations. Extend and can override SYSTEM rules for user-specific behaviors.
   456→
   457→**Loading:** Both files are concatenated at runtime. SYSTEM loads first, USER extends. Conflicts resolve in USER's favor.
   458→
   459→**When to read:** Reference steering rules when uncertain about behavioral expectations, after errors, or when user explicitly mentions rules.
   460→
   461→---
   462→
   463→## Documentation Reference
   464→
   465→Critical PAI documentation organized by domain. Load on-demand based on context.
   466→
   467→| Domain | Path | Purpose |
   468→|--------|------|---------|
   469→| **System Architecture** | `SYSTEM/PAISYSTEMARCHITECTURE.md` | Core PAI design and principles |
   470→| **Memory System** | `SYSTEM/MEMORYSYSTEM.md` | WORK, STATE, LEARNING directories |
   471→| **Skill System** | `SYSTEM/SKILLSYSTEM.md` | How skills work, structure, triggers |
   472→| **Hook System** | `SYSTEM/THEHOOKSYSTEM.md` | Event hooks, patterns, implementation |
   473→| **Agent System** | `SYSTEM/PAIAGENTSYSTEM.md` | Agent types, spawning, delegation |
   474→| **Delegation** | `SYSTEM/THEDELEGATIONSYSTEM.md` | Background work, parallelization |
   475→| **Browser Automation** | `SYSTEM/BROWSERAUTOMATION.md` | Playwright, screenshots, testing |
   476→| **CLI Architecture** | `SYSTEM/CLIFIRSTARCHITECTURE.md` | Command-line first principles |
   477→| **Notification System** | `SYSTEM/THENOTIFICATIONSYSTEM.md` | Voice, visual notifications |
   478→| **Tools Reference** | `SYSTEM/TOOLS.md` | Core tools inventory |
   479→
   480→**USER Context:** `USER/` contains personal data—identity, contacts, health, finances, projects. See `USER/README.md` for full index.
   481→
   482→**Project Routing:**
   483→
   484→| Trigger | Path | Purpose |
   485→|---------|------|---------|
   486→| "projects", "my projects", "project paths", "deploy" | `USER/PROJECTS/PROJECTS.md` | Technical project registry—paths, deployment, routing aliases |
   487→| "Telos", "life goals", "goals", "challenges" | `USER/TELOS/PROJECTS.md` | Life goals, challenges, predictions (Telos Life System) |

1→# CreateSkill Workflow
     2→
     3→Create a new skill following the canonical structure with proper TitleCase naming.
     4→
     5→## Voice Notification
     6→
     7→```bash
     8→curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8888/notify \
     9→  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    10→  -d '{"message": "Running the CreateSkill workflow in the CreateSkill skill to create new skill"}' \
    11→  > /dev/null 2>&1 &
    12→```
    13→
    14→Running the **CreateSkill** workflow in the **CreateSkill** skill to create new skill...
    15→
    16→## Step 1: Read the Authoritative Sources
    17→
    18→**REQUIRED FIRST:**
    19→
    20→1. Read the skill system documentation: `~/.claude/skills/PAI/SkillSystem.md`
    21→2. Read the canonical example: `~/.claude/skills/Art/SKILL.md`
    22→
    23→## Step 2: Understand the Request
    24→
    25→Ask the user:
    26→1. What does this skill do?
    27→2. What should trigger it?
    28→3. What workflows does it need?
    29→
    30→## Step 3: Determine TitleCase Names
    31→
    32→**All names must use TitleCase (PascalCase).**
    33→
    34→| Component | Format | Example |
    35→|-----------|--------|---------|
    36→| Skill directory | TitleCase | `Blogging`, `Daemon`, `CreateSkill` |
    37→| Workflow files | TitleCase.md | `Create.md`, `UpdateDaemonInfo.md` |
    38→| Reference docs | TitleCase.md | `ProsodyGuide.md`, `ApiReference.md` |
    39→| Tool files | TitleCase.ts | `ManageServer.ts` |
    40→| Help files | TitleCase.help.md | `ManageServer.help.md` |
    41→
    42→**Wrong naming (NEVER use):**
    43→- `create-skill`, `create_skill`, `CREATESKILL` → Use `CreateSkill`
    44→- `create.md`, `CREATE.md`, `create-info.md` → Use `Create.md`, `CreateInfo.md`
    45→
    46→## Step 4: Create the Skill Directory
    47→
    48→```bash
    49→mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills/[SkillName]/Workflows
    50→mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills/[SkillName]/Tools
    51→```
    52→
    53→**Example:**
    54→```bash
    55→mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills/Daemon/Workflows
    56→mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills/Daemon/Tools
    57→```
    58→
    59→## Step 5: Create SKILL.md
    60→
    61→Follow this exact structure:
    62→
    63→```yaml
    64→---
    65→name: SkillName
    66→description: [What it does]. USE WHEN [intent triggers using OR]. [Additional capabilities].
    67→---
    68→
    69→# SkillName
    70→
    71→[Brief description]
    72→
    73→## Voice Notification
    74→
    75→**When executing a workflow, do BOTH:**
    76→
    77→1. **Send voice notification**:
    78→   ```bash
    79→   curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8888/notify \
    80→     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    81→     -d '{"message": "Running WORKFLOWNAME in SKILLNAME"}' \
    82→     > /dev/null 2>&1 &
    83→   ```
    84→
    85→2. **Output text notification**:
    86→   ```
    87→   Running **WorkflowName** in **SkillName**...
    88→   ```
    89→
    90→**Full documentation:** `~/.claude/skills/PAI/SYSTEM/THENOTIFICATIONSYSTEM.md`
    91→
    92→## Workflow Routing
    93→

content.content:
1→# Custom Skill System
     2→
     3→**The MANDATORY configuration system for ALL PAI skills.**
     4→
     5→---
     6→
     7→## THIS IS THE AUTHORITATIVE SOURCE
     8→
     9→This document defines the **required structure** for every skill in the PAI system.
    10→
    11→**ALL skill creation MUST follow this structure** - including skills created by the CreateSkill skill.
    12→
    13→**"Canonicalize a skill"** = Restructure it to match this exact format, including TitleCase naming.
    14→
    15→If a skill does not follow this structure, it is not properly configured and will not work correctly.
    16→
    17→---
    18→
    19→## TitleCase Naming Convention (MANDATORY)
    20→
    21→**All naming in the skill system MUST use TitleCase (PascalCase).**
    22→
    23→| Component | Wrong | Correct |
    24→|-----------|-------|---------|
    25→| Skill directory | `createskill`, `create-skill`, `CREATE_SKILL` | `Createskill` or `CreateSkill` |
    26→| Workflow files | `create.md`, `update-info.md`, `SYNC_REPO.md` | `Create.md`, `UpdateInfo.md`, `SyncRepo.md` |
    27→| Reference docs | `prosody-guide.md`, `API_REFERENCE.md` | `ProsodyGuide.md`, `ApiReference.md` |
    28→| Tool files | `manage-server.ts`, `MANAGE_SERVER.ts` | `ManageServer.ts` |
    29→| Help files | `manage-server.help.md` | `ManageServer.help.md` |
    30→| YAML name | `name: create-skill` | `name: CreateSkill` |
    31→
    32→**TitleCase Rules:**
    33→- First letter of each word capitalized
    34→- No hyphens, underscores, or spaces
    35→- No ALL_CAPS or all_lowercase
    36→- Single words: first letter capital (e.g., `Blogging`, `Daemon`)
    37→- Multi-word: each word capitalized, no separator (e.g., `UpdateDaemonInfo`, `SyncRepo`)
    38→
    39→**Exception:** `SKILL.md` is always uppercase (convention for the main skill file).
    40→
    41→---
    42→
    43→## Personal vs System Skills (CRITICAL)
    44→
    45→**Skills are classified into two categories:**
    46→
    47→### System Skills (Shareable via PAI Packs)
    48→- Use **TitleCase** naming: `Browser`, `Research`, `Development`
    49→- Contain NO personal data (contacts, API keys, team members)
    50→- Reference `~/.claude/skills/PAI/USER/` for any personalization
    51→- Can be exported to the public PAI repository
    52→
    53→### Personal Skills (Never Shared)
    54→- Use **underscore + ALL CAPS** naming: `_BLOGGING`, `_METRICS`, `_CLICKUP`
    55→- Contain personal configuration, API keys, business-specific workflows
    56→- Will NEVER be pushed to public PAI
    57→- The underscore prefix makes them sort first and visually distinct
    58→
    59→**Personal Skills:** *(dynamically discovered)*
    60→
    61→Personal skills are identified by their `_ALLCAPS` naming convention. To list current personal skills:
    62→```bash
    63→ls -1 ~/.claude/skills/ | grep "^_"
    64→```
    65→
    66→This ensures documentation never drifts from reality. The underscore prefix ensures:
    67→- They sort first in directory listings
    68→- They are visually distinct from system skills
    69→- They are automatically excluded from PAI pack exports
    70→
    71→**Pattern for Personalization in System Skills:**
    72→System skills should reference PAI/USER files for personal data:
    73→```markdown
    74→## Configuration
    75→Personal configuration loaded from:
    76→- `~/.claude/skills/PAI/USER/CONTACTS.md` - Contact information
    77→- `~/.claude/skills/PAI/USER/TECHSTACKPREFERENCES.md` - Tech preferences
    78→```
    79→
    80→**NEVER hardcode personal data in system skills.**
    81→
    82→---
    83→
    84→## Skill Customization System
    85→
    86→**System skills (TitleCase) check for user customizations before executing.**
    87→
    88→**Personal skills (_ALLCAPS) do NOT use this system** - they already contain personal data directly and are never shared.
    89→
    90→### The Pattern
    91→
    92→All skills include this standard instruction block after the YAML frontmatter:
    93→
    94→```markdown
    95→## Customization
    96→
    97→**Before executing, check for user customizations at:**
    98→`~/.claude/skills/PAI/USER/SKILLCUSTOMIZATIONS/{SkillName}/`
    99→
   100→If this directory exists, load and apply:
   101→- `PREFERENCES.md` - User preferences and configuration
   102→- Additional files specific to the skill
   103→
   104→These define user-specific preferences. If the directory does not exist, proceed with skill defaults.
   105→```
   106→
   107→### Directory Structure
   108→
   109→```
   110→~/.claude/skills/PAI/USER/SKILLCUSTOMIZATIONS/
   111→├── README.md                    # Documentation for this system
   112→├── Art/                         # Art skill customizations
   113→│   ├── EXTEND.yaml              # Extension manifest
   114→│   ├── PREFERENCES.md           # Aesthetic preferences
   115→│   ├── CharacterSpecs.md        # Character design specs
   116→│   └── SceneConstruction.md     # Scene building guidelines
   117→├── Agents/                      # Agents skill customizations
   118→│   ├── EXTEND.yaml              # Extension manifest
   119→│   ├── PREFERENCES.md           # Named agent summary
   120→│   └── VoiceConfig.json         # ElevenLabs voice mappings
   121→├── FrontendDesign/              # FrontendDesign customizations
   122→│   ├── EXTEND.yaml              # Extension manifest
   123→│   └── PREFERENCES.md           # Design tokens, palette
   124→└── [SkillName]/                 # Any skill can have customizations
   125→    ├── EXTEND.yaml              # Required manifest
   126→    └── [config-files]           # Skill-specific configs
   127→```
   128→
   129→### EXTEND.yaml Manifest
   130→
   131→Every customization directory requires an EXTEND.yaml manifest:
   132→
   133→```yaml
   134→# EXTEND.yaml - Extension manifest
   135→---
   136→skill: SkillName                   # Must match skill name exactly
   137→extends:
   138→  - PREFERENCES.md                 # Files to load
   139→  - OtherConfig.md
   140→merge_strategy: override           # append | override | deep_merge
   141→enabled: true                      # Toggle customizations on/off
   142→description: "What this customization adds"
   143→```
   144→
   145→### Merge Strategies
   146→
   147→| Strategy | Behavior |
   148→|----------|----------|
   149→| `append` | Add items to existing config (default) |
   150→| `override` | Replace default behavior entirely |
   151→| `deep_merge` | Recursive merge of objects |
   152→
   153→### What Goes Where
   154→
   155→| Content Type | Location | Example |
   156→|--------------|----------|---------|
   157→| User preferences | `SKILLCUSTOMIZATIONS/{Skill}/PREFERENCES.md` | Art style, color palette |
   158→| Named configurations | `SKILLCUSTOMIZATIONS/{Skill}/[name].md` | Character specs, voice configs |
   159→| Skill logic | `skills/{Skill}/SKILL.md` | Generic, shareable skill code |
   160→
   161→### Creating a Customization
   162→
   163→1. **Create directory**: `mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills/PAI/USER/SKILLCUSTOMIZATIONS/SkillName`
   164→2. **Create EXTEND.yaml**: Define what files to load and merge strategy
   165→3. **Create PREFERENCES.md**: User preferences for this skill
   166→4. **Add additional files**: Any skill-specific configurations
   167→
   168→### Benefits
   169→
   170→- **Shareable Skills**: Skill files contain no personal data
   171→- **Centralized Preferences**: All customizations in one location
   172→- **Discoverable**: Easy to see which skills have customizations
   173→- **Toggleable**: Set `enabled: false` to disable customizations temporarily
   174→
   175→---
   176→
   177→## The Required Structure
   178→
   179→Every SKILL.md has two parts:
   180→
   181→### 1. YAML Frontmatter (Single-Line Description)
   182→
   183→```yaml
   184→---
   185→name: SkillName
   186→description: [What it does]. USE WHEN [intent triggers using OR]. [Additional capabilities].
   187→implements: Science              # Optional: declares Science Protocol compliance
   188→science_cycle_time: meso         # Optional: micro | meso | macro
   189→---
   190→```
   191→
   192→**Rules:**
   193→- `name` uses **TitleCase**
   194→- `description` is a **single line** (not multi-line with `|`)
   195→- `USE WHEN` keyword is **MANDATORY** (Claude Code parses this for skill activation)
   196→- Use intent-based triggers with `OR` for multiple conditions
   197→- Max 1024 characters (Anthropic hard limit)
   198→- **NO separate `triggers:` or `workflows:` arrays in YAML**
   199→
   200→### Science Protocol Compliance (Optional)
   201→
   202→Skills that involve systematic investigation, iteration, or evidence-based improvement can declare Science Protocol compliance:
   203→
   204→```yaml
   205→implements: Science
   206→science_cycle_time: meso
   207→```
   208→
   209→**What This Means:**
   210→- The skill embodies the scientific method: Goal → Observe → Hypothesize → Experiment → Measure → Analyze → Iterate
   211→- This is documentation of the mapping, not runtime coupling
   212→- Skills implement Science like classes implement interfaces—they follow the pattern independently
   213→
   214→**Cycle Time Options:**
   215→| Level | Cycle Time | Formality | Example Skills |
   216→|-------|------------|-----------|----------------|
   217→| `micro` | Seconds-Minutes | Implicit (internalized) | Most skills |
   218→| `meso` | Hours-Days | Explicit when stuck | Evals, Research, Development |
   219→| `macro` | Weeks-Months | Formal documentation | Major architecture work |
   220→
   221→**Skills That Implement Science:**
   222→- **Development** - TDD is Science (test = goal, code = experiment, pass/fail = analysis)
   223→- **Evals** - Prompt optimization through systematic experimentation
   224→- **Research** - Investigation through hypotheses and evidence gathering
   225→- **Council** - Debate as parallel hypothesis testing
   226→
   227→**See:** `~/.claude/skills/Science/Protocol.md` for the full protocol interface
   228→
   229→### 2. Markdown Body (Workflow Routing + Examples + Documentation)
   230→
   231→```markdown
   232→# SkillName
   233→
   234→[Brief description of what the skill does]
   235→
   236→## Voice Notification
   237→
   238→**When executing a workflow, do BOTH:**
   239→
   240→1. **Send voice notification**:
   241→   ```bash
   242→   curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8888/notify \
   243→     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
   244→     -d '{"message": "Running the WORKFLOWNAME workflow in the SKILLNAME skill to ACTION"}' \
   245→     > /dev/null 2>&1 &
   246→   ```
   247→
   248→2. **Output text notification**:
   249→   ```
   250→   Running the **WorkflowName** workflow in the **SkillName** skill to ACTION...
   251→   ```
   252→
   253→**Full documentation:** `~/.claude/skills/PAI/SYSTEM/THENOTIFICATIONSYSTEM.md`
   254→
   255→## Workflow Routing
   256→
   257→The notification announces workflow execution. The routing table tells Claude which workflow to execute:
   258→
   259→| Workflow | Trigger | File |
   260→|----------|---------|------|
   261→| **WorkflowOne** | "trigger phrase" | `Workflows/WorkflowOne.md` |
   262→| **WorkflowTwo** | "another trigger" | `Workflows/WorkflowTwo.md` |
   263→
   264→## Examples
   265→
   266→**Example 1: [Common use case]**
   267→```
   268→User: "[Typical user request]"
   269→→ Invokes WorkflowOne workflow
   270→→ [What skill does]
   271→→ [What user gets back]
   272→```
   273→
   274→**Example 2: [Another use case]**
   275→```
   276→User: "[Another typical request]"
   277→→ [Process]
   278→→ [Output]
   279→```
   280→
   281→## [Additional Sections]
   282→
   283→[Documentation, quick reference, critical paths, etc.]
   284→```
   285→
   286→**Workflow routing format:** Table with Workflow, Trigger, File columns
   287→- Workflow names in **TitleCase** matching file names
   288→- Simple trigger description
   289→- File path in backticks
   290→
   291→**When to show the workflow message:**
   292→- ONLY output the message when actually loading and executing a workflow file
   293→- If the skill handles the request directly without calling a workflow, do NOT show the message
   294→- The message indicates "I'm reading and following instructions from a workflow file"
   295→
   296→---
   297→
   298→## Dynamic Loading Pattern (Recommended for Large Skills)
   299→
   300→**Purpose:** Reduce context on skill invocation by keeping SKILL.md minimal and loading additional context files only when needed.

content.content:
300→**Purpose:** Reduce context on skill invocation by keeping SKILL.md minimal and loading additional context files only when needed.
   301→
   302→### How Loading Works
   303→
   304→**Session Startup:**
   305→- Only frontmatter (YAML) loads from all SKILL.md files for routing
   306→
   307→**Skill Invocation:**
   308→- Full SKILL.md body loads when skill is invoked
   309→- Additional .md context files load when referenced by workflows or called directly
   310→
   311→**Benefit:** Most skill invocations don't need all documentation - load only what workflows actually use.
   312→
   313→### The Pattern
   314→
   315→**SKILL.md** = Minimal routing + quick reference (30-50 lines)
   316→**Additional .md files** = Context files - SOPs for specific aspects (loaded on-demand)
   317→
   318→### Structure
   319→
   320→```
   321→skills/SkillName/
   322→├── SKILL.md                    # Minimal routing - loads on invocation
   323→├── Aesthetic.md                # Context file - SOP for aesthetic handling
   324→├── Examples.md                 # Context file - SOP for examples
   325→├── ApiReference.md             # Context file - SOP for API usage
   326→├── Tools.md                    # Context file - SOP for tool usage
   327→├── Workflows/                  # Workflow execution files
   328→│   ├── Create.md
   329→│   └── Update.md
   330→└── Tools/                      # Actual CLI tools
   331→    └── Generate.ts
   332→```
   333→
   334→### 🚨 CRITICAL: NO Context/ Subdirectory 🚨
   335→
   336→**NEVER create a Context/ or Docs/ subdirectory.**
   337→
   338→The additional .md files ARE the context files. They live **directly in the skill root directory** alongside SKILL.md.
   339→
   340→**WRONG (DO NOT DO THIS):**
   341→```
   342→skills/SkillName/
   343→├── SKILL.md
   344→└── Context/              ❌ NEVER CREATE THIS DIRECTORY
   345→    ├── Aesthetic.md
   346→    └── Examples.md
   347→```
   348→
   349→**CORRECT:**
   350→```
   351→skills/SkillName/
   352→├── SKILL.md
   353→├── Aesthetic.md          ✅ Context file in skill root
   354→└── Examples.md           ✅ Context file in skill root
   355→```
   356→
   357→**The skill directory itself IS the context.** Additional .md files are context files that provide SOPs for specific aspects of the skill's operation.
   358→
   359→### What Goes In SKILL.md (Minimal)
   360→
   361→Keep only these in SKILL.md:
   362→- ✅ YAML frontmatter with triggers
   363→- ✅ Brief description (1-2 lines)
   364→- ✅ Workflow routing table
   365→- ✅ Quick reference (3-5 bullet points)
   366→- ✅ Pointers to detailed docs via SkillSearch
   367→
   368→### What Goes In Additional .md Context Files (Loaded On-Demand)
   369→
   370→These are **additional SOPs** (Standard Operating Procedures) for specific aspects. They live in skill root and can reference Workflows/, Tools/, etc.
   371→
   372→Move these to separate context files in skill root:
   373→- ❌ Extended documentation → `Documentation.md`
   374→- ❌ API reference → `ApiReference.md`
   375→- ❌ Detailed examples → `Examples.md`
   376→- ❌ Tool documentation → `Tools.md`
   377→- ❌ Aesthetic guides → `Aesthetic.md`
   378→- ❌ Configuration details → `Configuration.md`
   379→
   380→**These are SOPs, not just docs.** They provide specific handling instructions for workflows to reference.
   381→
   382→### Example: Minimal SKILL.md
   383→
   384→```markdown
   385→---
   386→name: Art
   387→description: Visual content system. USE WHEN art, header images, visualizations, diagrams.
   388→---
   389→
   390→# Art Skill
   391→
   392→Complete visual content system using **charcoal architectural sketch** aesthetic.
   393→
   394→## Workflow Routing
   395→
   396→| Trigger | Workflow |
   397→|---------|----------|
   398→| Blog header/editorial | `Workflows/Essay.md` |
   399→| Technical diagram | `Workflows/TechnicalDiagrams.md` |
   400→| Mermaid flowchart | `Workflows/Mermaid.md` |
   401→
   402→## Quick Reference
   403→
   404→**Aesthetic:** Charcoal architectural sketch
   405→**Model:** nano-banana-pro
   406→**Output:** Always ~/Downloads/ first
   407→
   408→**Full Documentation:**
   409→- Aesthetic guide: `SkillSearch('art aesthetic')` → loads Aesthetic.md
   410→- Examples: `SkillSearch('art examples')` → loads Examples.md
   411→- Tools: `SkillSearch('art tools')` → loads Tools.md
   412→```
   413→
   414→### Loading Additional Context Files
   415→
   416→Workflows call SkillSearch to load context files as needed:
   417→
   418→```bash
   419→# In workflow files or SKILL.md
   420→SkillSearch('art aesthetic')    # Loads Aesthetic.md from skill root
   421→SkillSearch('art examples')     # Loads Examples.md from skill root
   422→SkillSearch('art tools')        # Loads Tools.md from skill root
   423→```
   424→
   425→Or reference them directly:
   426→```bash
   427→# Read specific context file
   428→Read ~/.claude/skills/Art/Aesthetic.md
   429→```
   430→
   431→Context files can reference workflows and tools:
   432→```markdown
   433→# Aesthetic.md (context file)
   434→
   435→Use the Essay workflow for blog headers: `Workflows/Essay.md`
   436→Generate images with: `bun Tools/Generate.ts`
   437→```
   438→
   439→### Benefits
   440→
   441→**Token Savings on Skill Invocation:**
   442→- Before: 150+ lines load when skill invoked
   443→- After: 40-50 lines load when skill invoked
   444→- Additional context loads only if workflows need it
   445→- Reduction: 70%+ token savings per invocation (when full docs not needed)
   446→
   447→**Improved Organization:**
   448→- SKILL.md = clean routing layer
   449→- Context files = SOPs for specific aspects
   450→- Workflows load only what they need
   451→- Easier to maintain and update
   452→
   453→### When To Use
   454→
   455→Use dynamic loading for skills with:
   456→- ✅ SKILL.md > 100 lines
   457→- ✅ Multiple documentation sections
   458→- ✅ Extensive API reference
   459→- ✅ Detailed examples
   460→- ✅ Tool documentation
   461→
   462→Don't bother for:
   463→- ❌ Simple skills (< 50 lines total)
   464→- ❌ Pure utility wrappers (use PAI/SYSTEM/TOOLS.md instead)
   465→- ❌ Skills that are already minimal
   466→
   467→---
   468→
   469→## Canonicalization
   470→
   471→**"Canonicalize a skill"** means restructuring it to match this document exactly.
   472→
   473→### When to Canonicalize
   474→
   475→- Skill has old YAML format (separate `triggers:` or `workflows:` arrays)
   476→- Skill uses non-TitleCase naming
   477→- Skill is missing `USE WHEN` in description
   478→- Skill lacks `## Examples` section
   479→- Skill has `backups/` inside its directory
   480→- Workflow routing uses old format
   481→
   482→### Canonicalization Checklist
   483→
   484→#### Naming (TitleCase)
   485→- [ ] Skill directory uses TitleCase
   486→- [ ] All workflow files use TitleCase
   487→- [ ] All reference docs use TitleCase
   488→- [ ] All tool files use TitleCase
   489→- [ ] Routing table names match file names exactly
   490→- [ ] YAML `name:` uses TitleCase
   491→
   492→#### YAML Frontmatter
   493→- [ ] Single-line `description` with embedded `USE WHEN`
   494→- [ ] No separate `triggers:` or `workflows:` arrays
   495→- [ ] Description uses intent-based language
   496→- [ ] Description under 1024 characters
   497→
   498→#### Markdown Body
   499→- [ ] `## Workflow Routing` section with table format
   500→- [ ] All workflow files have routing entries
   501→- [ ] `## Examples` section with 2-3 concrete patterns
   502→
   503→#### Structure
   504→- [ ] `tools/` directory exists (even if empty)
   505→- [ ] No `backups/` directory inside skill
   506→- [ ] Reference docs at skill root (not in Workflows/)
   507→- [ ] Workflows contain ONLY execution procedures
   508→
   509→### How to Canonicalize
   510→
   511→Use the Createskill skill's CanonicalizeSkill workflow:
   512→```
   513→~/.claude/skills/Createskill/Workflows/CanonicalizeSkill.md
   514→```
   515→
   516→Or manually:
   517→1. Rename files to TitleCase
   518→2. Update YAML frontmatter to single-line description
   519→3. Add `## Workflow Routing` table
   520→4. Add `## Examples` section
   521→5. Move backups to `~/.claude/MEMORY/Backups/`
   522→6. Verify against checklist
   523→
   524→---
   525→
   526→## Examples Section (REQUIRED)
   527→
   528→**Every skill MUST have an `## Examples` section** showing 2-3 concrete usage patterns.
   529→
   530→**Why Examples Matter:**
   531→- Anthropic research shows examples improve tool selection accuracy from 72% to 90%
   532→- Descriptions tell Claude WHEN to activate; examples show HOW the skill works
   533→- Claude learns the full input→behavior→output pattern, not just trigger keywords
   534→
   535→**Example Format:**
   536→```markdown
   537→## Examples
   538→
   539→**Example 1: [Use case name]**
   540→```
   541→User: "[Actual user request]"
   542→→ Invokes WorkflowName workflow
   543→→ [What the skill does - action 1]
   544→→ [What user receives back]
   545→```
   546→
   547→**Example 2: [Another use case]**
   548→```
   549→User: "[Different request pattern]"
   550→→ [Process steps]
   551→→ [Output/result]
   552→```
   553→```
   554→
   555→**Guidelines:**
   556→- Use 2-3 examples per skill (not more)
   557→- Show realistic user requests (natural language)
   558→- Include the workflow or action taken (TitleCase)
   559→- Show what output/result the user gets
   560→- Cover the most common use cases
   561→
   562→---
   563→
   564→## Intent Matching, Not String Matching
   565→
   566→We use **intent matching**, not exact phrase matching.
   567→
   568→**Example description:**
   569→```yaml
   570→description: Complete blog workflow. USE WHEN user mentions doing anything with their blog, website, site, including things like update, proofread, write, edit, publish, preview, blog posts, articles, headers, or website pages, etc.
   571→```
   572→
   573→**Key Principles:**
   574→- Use intent language: "user mentions", "user wants to", "including things like"
   575→- Don't list exact phrases in quotes
   576→- Cover the domain conceptually
   577→- Use `OR` to combine multiple trigger conditions
   578→
   579→---
   580→
   581→## Complete Canonical Example: Blogging Skill
   582→
   583→**Reference:** `~/.claude/skills/_BLOGGING/SKILL.md`
   584→
   585→```yaml
   586→---
   587→name: Blogging
   588→description: Complete blog workflow. USE WHEN user mentions doing anything with their blog, website, site, including things like update, proofread, write, edit, publish, preview, blog posts, articles, headers, or website pages, etc.
   589→---
   590→
   591→# Blogging
   592→
   593→Complete blog workflow.
   594→
   595→## Voice Notification
   596→
   597→**When executing a workflow, do BOTH:**
   598→
   599→1. **Send voice notification**:
   600→   ```bash
   601→   curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8888/notify \
   602→     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
   603→     -d '{"message": "Running WORKFLOWNAME in Blogging"}' \
   604→     > /dev/null 2>&1 &
   605→   ```
   606→
   607→2. **Output text notification**:
   608→   ```
   609→   Running the **WorkflowName** workflow in the **Blogging** skill to ACTION...
   610→   ```
   611→
   612→**Full documentation:** `~/.claude/skills/PAI/SYSTEM/THENOTIFICATIONSYSTEM.md`
   613→
   614→## Core Paths
   615→
   616→- **Blog posts:** `~/Projects/Website/cms/blog/`
   617→- **CMS root:** `~/Projects/Website/cms/`
   618→- **Images:** `~/Projects/Website/cms/public/images/`
   619→
   620→## Workflow Routing
   621→
   622→**When executing a workflow, also output this text:**
   623→
   624→```
   625→Running the **WorkflowName** workflow in the **Blogging** skill to ACTION...
   626→```
   627→
   628→| Workflow | Trigger | File |
   629→|----------|---------|------|
   630→| **Create** | "write a post", "new article" | `Workflows/Create.md` |
   631→| **Rewrite** | "rewrite this post" | `Workflows/Rewrite.md` |
   632→| **Publish** | "publish", "deploy" | `Workflows/Publish.md` |
   633→| **Open** | "preview", "open in browser" | `Workflows/Open.md` |
   634→| **Header** | "create header image" | `Workflows/Header.md` |
   635→
   636→## Examples
   637→
   638→**Example 1: Write new content**
   639→```
   640→User: "Write a post about AI agents for the blog"
   641→→ Invokes Create workflow
   642→→ Drafts content in scratchpad/
   643→→ Opens dev server preview at localhost:5173
   644→```
   645→
   646→**Example 2: Publish**
   647→```
   648→User: "Publish the AI agents post"
   649→→ Invokes Publish workflow
   650→→ Runs build validation
   651→→ Deploys to Cloudflare Pages
   652→```
   653→
   654→## Quick Reference
   655→
   656→- **Tech Stack:** VitePress + bun + Cloudflare Pages
   657→- **Package Manager:** bun (NEVER npm)
   658→- **Dev Server:** `http://localhost:5173`
   659→- **Live Site:** `https://example.com`
   660→```
   661→
   662→---
   663→
   664→## Directory Structure
   665→
   666→Every skill follows this structure:
   667→
   668→```
   669→SkillName/                    # TitleCase directory name
   670→├── SKILL.md                  # Main skill file (always uppercase)
   671→├── QuickStartGuide.md        # Context/reference files in root (TitleCase)
   672→├── DefenseMechanisms.md      # Context/reference files in root (TitleCase)
   673→├── Examples.md               # Context/reference files in root (TitleCase)
   674→├── Tools/                    # CLI tools (ALWAYS present, even if empty)
   675→│   ├── ToolName.ts           # TypeScript CLI tool (TitleCase)
   676→│   └── ToolName.help.md      # Tool documentation (TitleCase)
   677→└── Workflows/                # Work execution workflows (TitleCase)
   678→    ├── Create.md             # Workflow file
   679→    ├── UpdateInfo.md         # Workflow file
   680→    └── SyncRepo.md           # Workflow file
   681→```
   682→
   683→- **SKILL.md** - Contains single-line description in YAML, workflow routing and documentation in body
   684→- **Context files (in root)** - Documentation, guides, reference materials live in skill root, NOT in subdirectories (TitleCase names)
   685→- **Tools/** - CLI tools for automation (ALWAYS present directory, even if empty)
   686→- **Workflows/** - Contains work execution workflows ONLY (TitleCase names)
   687→- **NO Resources/ or Docs/ subdirectories** - Context files go in skill root
   688→
   689→---
   690→
   691→## Flat Folder Structure (MANDATORY)
   692→
   693→**CRITICAL: Keep folder structure FLAT - maximum 2 levels deep.**
   694→
   695→### The Rule
   696→
   697→Skills use a **flat hierarchy** - no deep nesting of subdirectories.
   698→
   699→**Maximum depth:** `skills/SkillName/Category/`
   700→
   701→### ✅ ALLOWED (2 levels max)
   702→
   703→```
   704→skills/OSINT/SKILL.md                           # Skill root
   705→skills/OSINT/Workflows/CompanyDueDiligence.md   # Workflow - one level deep
   706→skills/OSINT/Tools/Analyze.ts                   # Tool - one level deep
   707→skills/OSINT/CompanyTools.md                    # Context file - in root
   708→skills/OSINT/Examples.md                        # Context file - in root
   709→skills/Prompting/BeCreative.md                  # Templates in Prompting root
   710→skills/Prompting/StoryExplanation.md            # Templates in Prompting root
   711→skills/PromptInjection/DefenseMechanisms.md     # Context file - in root
   712→skills/PromptInjection/QuickStartGuide.md       # Context file - in root
   713→```
   714→
   715→### ❌ FORBIDDEN (Too deep OR wrong location)
   716→
   717→```
   718→skills/OSINT/Resources/Examples.md              # Context files go in root, NOT Resources/
   719→skills/OSINT/Docs/CompanyTools.md               # Context files go in root, NOT Docs/
   720→skills/OSINT/Templates/Primitives/Extract.md    # THREE levels - NO
   721→skills/OSINT/Workflows/Company/DueDiligence.md  # THREE levels - NO (use CompanyDueDiligence.md instead)
   722→skills/Prompting/Templates/BeCreative.md        # Templates in root, NOT Templates/ subdirectory
   723→skills/Research/Workflows/Analysis/Deep.md      # THREE levels - NO
   724→```
   725→
   726→### Why Flat Structure
   727→
   728→1. **Discoverability** - Easy to find files with simple `ls` or `grep`
   729→2. **Simplicity** - Less cognitive overhead navigating directories
   730→3. **Speed** - Faster file operations without deep traversal
   731→4. **Maintainability** - Harder to create organizational complexity
   732→5. **Consistency** - Every skill follows same simple pattern
   733→
   734→### Allowed Subdirectories
   735→
   736→**ONLY these subdirectories are allowed:**
   737→
   738→1. **Workflows/** - Execution workflows ONLY
   739→   - All workflows go directly in `Workflows/`, NO subcategories
   740→   - Correct: `Workflows/CompanyDueDiligence.md`
   741→   - Wrong: `Workflows/Company/DueDiligence.md`
   742→
   743→2. **Tools/** - Executable scripts/tools ONLY
   744→   - CLI tools, automation scripts
   745→   - Correct: `Tools/Analyze.ts`
   746→   - Wrong: `Tools/Analysis/Analyze.ts`
   747→
   748→**Templates (Prompting skill only):**
   749→- Templates live in `skills/Prompting/` root, NOT nested
   750→- Correct: `skills/Prompting/BeCreative.md`
   751→- Wrong: `skills/Prompting/Templates/BeCreative.md`
   752→
   753→### Context/Resource Files Go in Skill Root
   754→
   755→**CRITICAL RULE: Documentation, guides, reference materials, and context files live in the skill ROOT directory, NOT in subdirectories.**
   756→
   757→❌ **WRONG** - Don't create subdirectories for context files:
   758→```
   759→skills/SkillName/Resources/Guide.md          # NO - no Resources/ subdirectory
   760→skills/SkillName/Docs/Reference.md           # NO - no Docs/ subdirectory
   761→skills/SkillName/Guides/QuickStart.md        # NO - no Guides/ subdirectory
   762→```
   763→
   764→✅ **CORRECT** - Put context files directly in skill root:
   765→```
   766→skills/SkillName/Guide.md                    # YES - in root
   767→skills/SkillName/Reference.md                # YES - in root
   768→skills/SkillName/QuickStart.md               # YES - in root
   769→skills/SkillName/DefenseMechanisms.md        # YES - in root
   770→skills/SkillName/ApiDocumentation.md         # YES - in root
   771→```
   772→
   773→**Exceptions:** Workflows/ and Tools/ subdirectories only. Everything else goes in the root.
   774→
   775→### Migration Rule
   776→
   777→If you encounter nested structures deeper than 2 levels:
   778→1. Flatten immediately
   779→2. Move files up to proper level
   780→3. Rename files for clarity if needed (e.g., `CompanyDueDiligence.md` instead of `Company/DueDiligence.md`)
   781→4. Update all references
   782→
   783→---
   784→
   785→## Workflow-to-Tool Integration
   786→
   787→**Workflows should map user intent to tool flags, not hardcode single invocation patterns.**
   788→
   789→When a workflow calls a CLI tool, it should:
   790→1. **Interpret user intent** from the request
   791→2. **Consult flag mapping tables** to determine appropriate flags
   792→3. **Construct the CLI command** with selected flags
   793→4. **Execute and handle results**
   794→
   795→### Intent-to-Flag Mapping Tables
   796→
   797→Workflows should include tables that map natural language intent to CLI flags:
   798→
   799→```markdown

---
name: Browser
description: Debug-first browser automation with always-on visibility. Console logs, network requests, and errors captured by default. USE WHEN browser, screenshot, debug web, verify UI, troubleshoot frontend.
version: 2.0.0
---

## Customization

**Before executing, check for user customizations at:**
`~/.claude/skills/PAI/USER/SKILLCUSTOMIZATIONS/Browser/`

If this directory exists, load and apply any PREFERENCES.md, configurations, or resources found there. These override default behavior. If the directory does not exist, proceed with skill defaults.


## 🚨 MANDATORY: Voice Notification (REQUIRED BEFORE ANY ACTION)

**You MUST send this notification BEFORE doing anything else when this skill is invoked.**

1. **Send voice notification**:
   ```bash
   curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8888/notify \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"message": "Running the WORKFLOWNAME workflow in the Browser skill to ACTION"}' \
     > /dev/null 2>&1 &
   ```

2. **Output text notification**:
   ```
   Running the **WorkflowName** workflow in the **Browser** skill to ACTION...
   ```

**This is not optional. Execute this curl command immediately upon skill invocation.**

# Browser v2.0.0 - Debug-First Browser Automation

**Debugging visibility by DEFAULT.** Console logs, network requests, and errors are always captured. No opt-in required.

---

## Philosophy

Debugging shouldn't be opt-in. Like good logging frameworks - you don't turn on logging when you have a problem, you have it enabled from the start so the data exists when problems occur.

**Headless by default.** All automation runs in headless mode. When the user says "show me" or wants to see what the assistant is seeing, open the URL in their preferred browser from `~/.claude/skills/PAI/USER/TECHSTACKPREFERENCES.md`:

```bash
# Open URL in user's preferred browser
open -a "$BROWSER" "<url>"  # BROWSER from tech stack prefs
```

**v2.0.0 Changes:**
- Session auto-starts on first use (no explicit `session start`)
- Console and network capture always enabled
- Diagnostic output included by default
- 30-minute idle timeout (auto-cleanup)
- New primary command: `Browse.ts <url>` for full diagnostics

---

## Quick Start

```bash
# Navigate with full diagnostics (PRIMARY COMMAND)
bun run ~/.claude/skills/Browser/Tools/Browse.ts https://example.com

# Output:
# 📸 Screenshot: /tmp/browse-1704614400.png
# 🔴 Console Errors (2): ...
# 🌐 Failed Requests (1): ...
# 📊 Network: 34 requests | 1.2MB | avg 120ms
# ✅ Page: "Example" loaded successfully
```

Session auto-starts. No setup needed.

---

## Commands

### Primary - Navigate with Diagnostics

```bash
bun run Browse.ts <url>
```

Navigates to URL, takes screenshot, and reports:
- Console errors and warnings
- Failed network requests (4xx, 5xx)
- Network statistics
- Page load status

### Query Commands

```bash
bun run Browse.ts errors      # Console errors only
bun run Browse.ts warnings    # Console warnings only
bun run Browse.ts console     # All console output
bun run Browse.ts network     # All network activity
bun run Browse.ts failed      # Failed requests only (4xx, 5xx)
```

1→---
     2→name: SECUpdates
     3→description: Security news aggregation from tldrsec, no.security, and other sources. USE WHEN security news, security updates, what's new in security, breaches, security research, sec updates. SkillSearch('secupdates') for docs.
     4→context: fork
     5→---
     6→
     7→## Customization
     8→
     9→**Before executing, check for user customizations at:**
    10→`~/.claude/skills/PAI/USER/SKILLCUSTOMIZATIONS/SECUpdates/`
    11→
    12→If this directory exists, load and apply any PREFERENCES.md, configurations, or resources found there. These override default behavior. If the directory does not exist, proceed with skill defaults.
    13→
    14→## Voice Notification (REQUIRED)
    15→
    16→**Send this notification BEFORE doing anything else:**
    17→
    18→```bash
    19→curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8888/notify \
    20→  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    21→  -d '{"message": "Checking security updates from sources"}' \
    22→  > /dev/null 2>&1 &
    23→```
    24→
    25→---
    26→
    27→# SECUpdates Skill
    28→
    29→**Purpose:** Aggregate security news from multiple sources into crisp, ranked updates across three categories.
    30→
    31→## Sources
    32→
    33→| Source | URL | Type |
    34→|--------|-----|------|
    35→| **tl;dr sec** | https://tldrsec.com | Newsletter/RSS - comprehensive security roundup |
    36→| **No Security** | https://no.security | Caleb Sima's security insights |
    37→| **Krebs on Security** | https://krebsonsecurity.com | Investigative security journalism |
    38→| **The Hacker News** | https://thehackernews.com | Security news and analysis |
    39→| **Schneier on Security** | https://schneier.com | Bruce Schneier's security blog |
    40→| **Risky Business** | https://risky.biz | Security podcast/news |
    41→
    42→**Custom sources:** Add to `USER/SKILLCUSTOMIZATIONS/SECUpdates/sources.json`
    43→
    44→---
    45→
    46→## Output Format
    47→
    48→**Maximum 32 items total across all categories, ranked by importance within each.**
    49→
    50→```markdown
    51→# Security Updates
    52→**Generated:** [timestamp]
    53→**Sources Checked:** [list]
    54→**Period:** Since [last check date]
    55→
    56→---
    57→
    58→## 🔴 Security News (Breaches & Incidents)
    59→*Hacks, breaches, exploits in the wild, incidents*
    60→
    61→1. **[Headline]** - [1-2 sentence summary]. [Source]
    62→2. **[Headline]** - [1-2 sentence summary]. [Source]
    63→...
    64→
    65→---
    66→
    67→## 🔬 Security Research
    68→*New vulnerabilities, CVEs, techniques, papers*
    69→
    70→1. **[Title]** - [1-2 sentence summary]. [Source]
    71→2. **[Title]** - [1-2 sentence summary]. [Source]
    72→...
    73→
    74→---
    75→
    76→## 💡 Security Ideas
    77→*Opinions, strategies, industry trends, career*
    78→
    79→1. **[Title]** - [1-2 sentence summary]. [Source]
    80→2. **[Title]** - [1-2 sentence summary]. [Source]
    81→...
    82→
    83→---
    84→
    85→## 📊 Summary
    86→| Category | Count | Top Item |
    87→|----------|-------|----------|
    88→| News | X | [headline] |
    89→| Research | X | [title] |
    90→| Ideas | X | [title] |
    91→
    92→**Total:** X/32 items | **Next check:** Run `/secupdates` anytime
    93→```
    94→
    95→---
    96→
    97→## Category Definitions
    98→
    99→### 🔴 Security News (Breaches & Incidents)
   100→- Data breaches and leaks
   101→- Active exploits and attacks
   102→- Ransomware incidents
   103→- State-sponsored attacks
   104→- Major vulnerability exploitations
   105→- Company security incidents
   106→
   107→### 🔬 Security Research
   108→- New CVEs and vulnerabilities
   109→- Security research papers
   110→- New attack techniques
   111→- Tool releases
   112→- Vulnerability disclosures
   113→- Bug bounty findings
   114→
   115→### 💡 Security Ideas
   116→- Industry trends and analysis
   117→- Security strategy and opinions
   118→- Career and hiring trends
   119→- Regulatory and compliance news
   120→- Security culture and practices
   121→- Predictions and forecasts
   122→
   123→---
   124→
   125→## Ranking Criteria
   126→
   127→Within each category, rank items by:
   128→
   129→1. **Impact** - How many people/systems affected?
   130→2. **Recency** - How new is this?
   131→3. **Actionability** - Can reader do something about it?
   132→4. **Novelty** - Is this genuinely new information?
   133→
   134→---
   135→
   136→## State Tracking
   137→
   138→**State file:** `State/last-check.json`
   139→
   140→```json
   141→{
   142→  "last_check_timestamp": "2026-01-22T12:00:00.000Z",
   143→  "sources": {
   144→    "tldrsec": {
   145→      "last_hash": "abc123",
   146→      "last_checked": "2026-01-22T12:00:00.000Z",
   147→      "last_title": "tl;dr sec #XXX"
   148→    },
   149→    "nosecurity": {
   150→      "last_hash": "def456",
   151→      "last_checked": "2026-01-22T12:00:00.000Z"
   152→    }
   153→  }
   154→}
   155→```
   156→
   157→**On each run:**
   158→1. Load last-check.json
   159→2. Fetch each source
   160→3. Compare content hash to detect new items
   161→4. Only include items newer than last check
   162→5. Update state file after successful run
   163→
   164→---
   165→
   166→## Process Flow
   167→
   168→### Step 1: Check State
   169→```bash
   170→# Read last check timestamp
   171→cat ~/.claude/skills/SECUpdates/State/last-check.json
   172→```
   173→
   174→### Step 2: Fetch Sources (Parallel)
   175→
   176→Launch parallel agents to fetch each source:
   177→
   178→| Agent | Source | Method |
   179→|-------|--------|--------|
   180→| Agent 1 | tldrsec.com | WebFetch latest newsletter |
   181→| Agent 2 | no.security | WebFetch recent posts |
   182→| Agent 3 | krebsonsecurity.com | WebFetch recent articles |
   183→| Agent 4 | thehackernews.com | WebFetch headlines |
   184→| Agent 5 | schneier.com | WebFetch recent posts |
   185→
   186→### Step 3: Parse & Categorize
   187→
   188→For each item found:
   189→1. Determine category (News/Research/Ideas)
   190→2. Extract headline and 1-2 sentence summary
   191→3. Note source
   192→4. Assess importance score
   193→
   194→### Step 4: Rank & Limit
   195→
   196→1. Sort each category by importance
   197→2. Take top items until 32 total
   198→3. Distribute reasonably (aim for ~10-12 per category if available)
   199→
   200→### Step 5: Output & Update State
   201→
   202→1. Generate formatted output
   203→2. Write updated state to last-check.json
   204→

name: SECUpdates
description: Security news aggregation from tldrsec, no.security, and other sources. USE WHEN security news, security updates, what's new in security, breaches, security research, sec updates. SkillSearch('secupdates') for docs.
context: fork
---

## Customization

**Before executing, check for user customizations at:**
`~/.claude/skills/PAI/USER/SKILLCUSTOMIZATIONS/SECUpdates/`

If this directory exists, load and apply any PREFERENCES.md, configurations, or resources found there. These override default behavior. If the directory does not exist, proceed with skill defaults.

## Voice Notification (REQUIRED)

**Send this notification BEFORE doing anything else:**

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8888/notify \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message": "Checking security updates from sources"}' \
  > /dev/null 2>&1 &
```

---

# SECUpdates Skill

**Purpose:** Aggregate security news from multiple sources into crisp, ranked updates across three categories.

## Sources

| Source | URL | Type |
|--------|-----|------|
| **tl;dr sec** | https://tldrsec.com | Newsletter/RSS - comprehensive security roundup |
| **No Security** | https://no.security | Caleb Sima's security insights |
| **Krebs on Security** | https://krebsonsecurity.com | Investigative security journalism |
| **The Hacker News** | https://thehackernews.com | Security news and analysis |
| **Schneier on Security** | https://schneier.com | Bruce Schneier's security blog |
| **Risky Business** | https://risky.biz | Security podcast/news |

**Custom sources:** Add to `USER/SKILLCUSTOMIZATIONS/SECUpdates/sources.json`

---

## Output Format

**Maximum 32 items total across all categories, ranked by importance within each.**

```markdown
# Security Updates
**Generated:** [timestamp]
**Sources Checked:** [list]
**Period:** Since [last check date]

---

## 🔴 Security News (Breaches & Incidents)
*Hacks, breaches, exploits in the wild, incidents*

1. **[Headline]** - [1-2 sentence summary]. [Source]
2. **[Headline]** - [1-2 sentence summary]. [Source]
...

---

## 🔬 Security Research
*New vulnerabilities, CVEs, techniques, papers*

1. **[Title]** - [1-2 sentence summary]. [Source]
2. **[Title]** - [1-2 sentence summary]. [Source]
...

---

## 💡 Security Ideas
*Opinions, strategies, industry trends, career*

1. **[Title]** - [1-2 sentence summary]. [Source]
2. **[Title]** - [1-2 sentence summary]. [Source]
...

---

## 📊 Summary
| Category | Count | Top Item |
|----------|-------|----------|
| News | X | [headline] |
| Research | X | [title] |
| Ideas | X | [title] |

**Total:** X/32 items | **Next check:** Run `/secupdates` anytime
```

---

## Category Definitions

### 🔴 Security News (Breaches & Incidents)
- Data breaches and leaks
- Active exploits and attacks
- Ransomware incidents
- State-sponsored attacks
- Major vulnerability exploitations
- Company security incidents

### 🔬 Security Research
- New CVEs and vulnerabilities
- Security research papers
- New attack techniques
- Tool releases
- Vulnerability disclosures
- Bug bounty findings

### 💡 Security Ideas
- Industry trends and analysis
- Security strategy and opinions
- Career and hiring trends
- Regulatory and compliance news
- Security culture and practices
- Predictions and forecasts

---

## Ranking Criteria

Within each category, rank items by:

1. **Impact** - How many people/systems affected?
2. **Recency** - How new is this?
3. **Actionability** - Can reader do something about it?
4. **Novelty** - Is this genuinely new information?

---

## State Tracking

**State file:** `State/last-check.json`

```json
{
  "last_check_timestamp": "2026-01-22T12:00:00.000Z",
  "sources": {
    "tldrsec": {
      "last_hash": "abc123",
      "last_checked": "2026-01-22T12:00:00.000Z",
      "last_title": "tl;dr sec #XXX"
    },
    "nosecurity": {
      "last_hash": "def456",
      "last_checked": "2026-01-22T12:00:00.000Z"
    }
  }
}
```

**On each run:**
1. Load last-check.json
2. Fetch each source
3. Compare content hash to detect new items
4. Only include items newer than last check
5. Update state file after successful run

---

## Process Flow

### Step 1: Check State
```bash
# Read last check timestamp
cat ~/.claude/skills/SECUpdates/State/last-check.json
```

### Step 2: Fetch Sources (Parallel)

Launch parallel agents to fetch each source:

| Agent | Source | Method |
|-------|--------|--------|
| Agent 1 | tldrsec.com | WebFetch latest newsletter |
| Agent 2 | no.security | WebFetch recent posts |
| Agent 3 | krebsonsecurity.com | WebFetch recent articles |
| Agent 4 | thehackernews.com | WebFetch headlines |
| Agent 5 | schneier.com | WebFetch recent posts |

### Step 3: Parse & Categorize

For each item found:
1. Determine category (News/Research/Ideas)
2. Extract headline and 1-2 sentence summary
3. Note source
4. Assess importance score

### Step 4: Rank & Limit

1. Sort each category by importance
2. Take top items until 32 total
3. Distribute reasonably (aim for ~10-12 per category if available)

### Step 5: Output & Update State

1. Generate formatted output
2. Write updated state to last-check.json

---

## Workflow Routing

| Workflow | Trigger | File |
|----------|---------|------|
| **Update** | "security updates", "sec updates", "/secupdates", "what's new in security" | `Workflows/Update.md` |

**Default:** Run the Update workflow.

---

## Key Principles

1. **Crisp** - 1-2 sentences per item, no fluff
2. **Ranked** - Most important first within each category
3. **Categorized** - Clear separation of News/Research/Ideas
4. **Deduplicated** - Same story from multiple sources = one entry
5. **Limited** - Max 32 items total, quality over quantity
6. **Stateful** - Track what's been seen, only show new items

---

## Example Output

```markdown
# Security Updates
**Generated:** 2026-01-22 12:09 PST
**Sources Checked:** tldrsec, no.security, Krebs, THN, Schneier
**Period:** Since 2026-01-20

---

## 🔴 Security News (Breaches & Incidents)

1. **Microsoft Azure Breach Exposes 2M Customer Records** - Misconfigured storage blob allowed unauthorized access to customer data including emails and phone numbers. [Krebs]
2. **LockBit 4.0 Ransomware Hits Healthcare Chain** - 15 hospitals affected, patient data encrypted, $10M ransom demanded. [THN]
3. **Ivanti VPN Zero-Day Actively Exploited** - CVE-2026-XXXX being used by Chinese APT groups against government targets. [tldrsec]

---

## 🔬 Security Research

1. **New Spectre Variant Bypasses All Mitigations** - Researchers demonstrate "Spectre-NG" affecting Intel and AMD processors, no patch available. [tldrsec]
2. **OAuth Token Theft via Browser Extension** - Novel technique allows stealing tokens from any site using malicious extension. [no.security]
3. **SSRF in AWS IMDSv2** - Bypass discovered in metadata service protections. [tldrsec]

---

## 💡 Security Ideas

1. **The Death of Perimeter Security** - Caleb Sima argues zero-trust is no longer optional after recent breaches. [no.security]
2. **CISO Burnout at All-Time High** - Survey shows 70% considering leaving the field within 2 years. [tldrsec]
3. **AI-Generated Phishing Now Indistinguishable** - Schneier on the implications of LLM-powered social engineering. [Schneier]

---

## 📊 Summary
| Category | Count | Top Item |
|----------|-------|----------|
| News | 3 | Microsoft Azure Breach |
| Research | 3 | New Spectre Variant |
| Ideas | 3 | Death of Perimeter Security |

**Total:** 9/32 items | **Next check:** Run `/secupdates` anytime
```

---

## Anti-Patterns

| ❌ Bad | ✅ Good |
|--------|---------|
| Long paragraph summaries | 1-2 crisp sentences |
| "Read more at..." | Summary + source attribution |
| Unranked list dumps | Importance-ordered items |
| 50+ items | Max 32, quality curated |
| Mixing categories | Clear News/Research/Ideas separation |
| Old news mixed with new | Only items since last check |

---
name: Triage
description: Fetch, categorize, and present GitHub issues for work selection
---

# Triage Workflow

## Step 1: Voice Notification

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8888/notify \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message": "Fetching GitHub issues for triage"}' \
  > /dev/null 2>&1 &
```

## Step 2: Determine Repository

**Priority order:**
1. If user passed a repo argument (e.g., `/issues danielmiessler/fabric`), use that
2. If current directory has a git remote, extract owner/repo from `git remote -v`
3. Fall back to `danielmiessler/PAI`

```bash
# Try git remote first
REPO=$(git remote get-url origin 2>/dev/null | sed -E 's#.*(github\.com[:/])([^/]+/[^/.]+)(\.git)?$#\2#')
# If empty, use default
REPO=${REPO:-danielmiessler/PAI}
echo "Using repo: $REPO"
```

## Step 3: Fetch Issues

Fetch open issues with full metadata:

```bash
gh issue list --repo "$REPO" --state open --limit 30 \
  --json number,title,labels,createdAt,comments,assignees,body
```

## Step 4: Categorize and Present

Parse the JSON output and categorize each issue:

### Categories

| Category | Icon | Matching labels or title patterns |
|----------|------|-----------------------------------|
| **Bugs** | `[BUG]` | label: `bug`, title contains: "Bug:", "Fix:", "fix:", "regression", "broken", "fails", "error" |
| **Enhancements** | `[ENH]` | label: `enhancement`, `feature`, title contains: "feat:", "Feature", "Enhancement", "Add", "Improve" |
| **Other** | `[OTH]` | Everything else |

### Display Format

Present a categorized summary table:

```markdown
## GitHub Issues: {owner}/{repo}
**Open:** {count} | **Fetched:** {date}

### [BUG] Bugs ({count})
| # | Title | Age | Comments |
|---|-------|-----|----------|
| #699 | plansDirectory: tilde in path not resolved | 2h | 0 |
| ... | ... | ... | ... |

### [ENH] Enhancements ({count})
| # | Title | Age | Comments |
|---|-------|-----|----------|
| #694 | Installer should set PAI_DIR to match CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR | 4h | 0 |
| ... | ... | ... | ... |

### [OTH] Other ({count})
| # | Title | Age | Comments |
|---|-------|-----|----------|
| ... | ... | ... | ... |
```

**Age formatting:** Show human-readable age (e.g., "2h", "1d", "3d", "1w").

**Sort within each category:** By comment count (most discussed first), then by recency.

## Step 5: Triage Selection

Use `AskUserQuestion` to present the top 4 most actionable issues as selectable options. Prioritize:
1. Bugs with community comments (signal: people care)
2. Recent bugs (likely relevant to current state)
3. Enhancements with comments
4. Everything else by recency

```
AskUserQuestion:
  question: "Which issue do you want to work on?"
  header: "Issue"
  options:
    - label: "#698 - Algorithm executes config changes without approval"
      description: "Bug - 1 comment, 2h old. Config modification gate needed."
    - label: "#697 - Version file mismatch"
      description: "Bug - 1 comment, 3h old. LATEST references non-existent version."
    - label: "#691 - Missing hook scripts"
      description: "Bug - 1 comment, 5h old. 7 hooks not wired in settings.json."
    - label: "#690 - Selective context loading"
      description: "Enhancement - 0 comments, 5h old. Reduce 83KB base context."
```

(The above is an example — generate dynamically from actual fetched data.)

## Step 6: Load Selected Issue

When the user selects an issue:

1. Fetch the full issue body and all comments:
   ```bash
   gh issue view {number} --repo "$REPO" --json title,body,comments,labels,assignees,createdAt
   ```

2. Present the full issue with:
   - Complete description/body
   - All comments (summarized if >5)
   - Suggested action plan based on issue type:
     - **Bug:** Reproduce -> Root cause -> Fix -> Test -> Close
     - **Enhancement:** Design -> Implement -> Test -> Close
     - **Other:** Assess -> Act -> Close

3. Ask if the user wants to proceed with the suggested plan or take a different approach.

---

## Notes

- The skill does NOT modify issues (no auto-assign, no label changes) — it's read-only triage
- The user decides what to work on; the skill just presents the information clearly
- If the repo has labels, use them for categorization; if not, fall back to title-based heuristics
- Always show the total count of open issues even if only displaying the first 30

     2→name: Triage
     3→description: Fetch, categorize, and present GitHub issues for work selection

     5→
     6→# Triage Workflow
     7→
